title: Double-drift: perception vs saccades (Lisi & Cavanagh 2015)
summary: Lisi & Cavanagh (2015), Experiment 1. A Gabor 10 dva right of fixation moves back and forth on a 3 dva path while its grating, whose stripes run along the path, drifts across it and reverses with every pass; seen in the periphery, an oblique path looks close to vertical. In the perceptual task the observer reports whether the path leans left or right of vertical while interleaved staircases vary the physical orientation, giving each participant's perceived-vertical orientations. In the saccade task those orientations are shown with and without the internal drift, and the observer saccades to the Gabor when the fixation dot goes off; the Gabor is removed at saccade onset. The question is whether the landings follow the physical path or the perceived one.
references: Lisi, M., & Cavanagh, P. (2015). Dissociation between the perceptual and saccadic localization of moving objects. Current Biology, 25(19), 2535-2540. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2015.08.021
Watson, A. B., & Pelli, D. G. (1983). QUEST: A Bayesian adaptive psychometric method. Perception & Psychophysics, 33(2), 113-120.
Watson, A. B. (2017). QUEST+: A general multidimensional Bayesian adaptive psychometric method. Journal of Vision, 17(3):10.
Engbert, R., & Mergenthaler, K. (2006). Microsaccades are triggered by low retinal image slip. PNAS, 103(18), 7192-7197.

deviations.here: Experiment 1 only: both of its tasks
deviations.original: Experiment 1 (perceptual task, saccade task) and Experiment 2 (mid-path gap, jump direction judgement)
deviations.reason: The comparison of perceived path orientation and saccade landings is Experiment 1; Experiment 2 (the position-vs-direction test) is a separate design and is not built here.

deviations.original: MATLAB with the Psychophysics and EyeLink toolboxes on an Apple computer

deviations.here: The rig's gamma-linearised display at its measured refresh rate (the example rig says 120 Hz); background = the display's mid-grey, whose luminance the software does not set
deviations.original: Gamma-linearised Compaq P1220 CRT at 120 Hz; uniform grey background of 5.3 cd/m2
deviations.reason: Hardware is the lab's. The rig file asks for gamma linearisation and for the mid-grey to be measured with a photometer; background_cd_m2 records the paper's value.

deviations.here: alhazen's QUEST+ (Watson 2017) with one free parameter (the threshold) and the same log-Weibull psychometric family, four staircases picked at random each trial
deviations.original: Multiple interleaved QUEST staircases (Watson & Pelli 1983) converging on 50% 'right' reports
deviations.reason: alhazen ships QUEST+, not QUEST. QUEST+ places each trial by minimum expected entropy instead of at the threshold estimate, so placements differ; the PSE is fitted afterwards to every trial, as in the paper.

deviations.here: Until the response or 30 s; a trial with no response is re-served
deviations.reason: An alhazen response window needs a deadline; 30 s is ten motion cycles.

deviations.here: Online, at the display rate: onset = gaze leaving the 2 dva fixation window, landing = first new sample slower than 30 dva/s after leaving (alhazen StimulusResponse and LandingSample); the EyeLink still records 1 kHz samples to its EDF
deviations.original: Onset and offset detected offline from 1 kHz samples (Engbert & Mergenthaler 2006)
deviations.reason: alhazen measures saccades online. The window exit comes a few ms after true onset (the Gabor moves 2 dva/s, so its position at 'onset' is off by a few hundredths of a dva); an offline reanalysis of the EDF can replace these columns.

deviations.here: Removed from the frame after the one on which gaze is first read outside the window (up to one extra frame, 8.3 ms at 120 Hz)
deviations.original: Removed as soon as gaze was detected outside the 2 dva window
deviations.reason: alhazen's StimulusResponse still draws the stimulus on the departure frame.

tasks.title: Perceptual task: left or right of vertical?
tasks.summary: Fixate; after 400-600 ms the double-drift Gabor moves on its path until a left or right arrow key reports its tilt; a look away or blink aborts and repeats the trial.
